title: Behold the Sun, How Bright
description: Behold the Sun, How Bright in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Moore wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 170, “Christianity”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold the sun, how bright From yon-der east he springs, As if the soul of life and light Were breath-ing from his wings.

lines: As if the soul of life and light
So fresh the dreaming world awoke
But, O, how dim, how pale, were those,
So truth lent many a ray,
But, Lord, how faint, how cold, were they,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Thomas Moore died in 1852.
credits: Words by Thomas Moore (1779–1852), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
